ECE 6390 / Antennas and arrays

Dish and pointing

From the figure to the physics

Fig. 1 shows the connection between aperture size, gain, beamwidth and pointing tolerance.

A circular dish has physical area πD²/4 and effective aperture Aₑ = ηₐπD²/4. With the stated aperture-efficiency convention, G = 4πAₑ/λ² = ηₐ(πD/λ)².

At fixed wavelength and efficiency, doubling diameter multiplies gain by four and approximately halves main-beam width. The supplied class width estimate is ΘHP ≈ √(33000/G) degrees, using linear gain.

The near-main-beam Gaussian pointing estimate is L ≈ 12(δ/ΘHP)² dB. A narrower beam makes a fixed angular pointing error more consequential. This approximation does not represent distant sidelobes or nulls.

Example

An offset δ = ΘHP/2 gives approximately 3 dB pointing loss in the Gaussian model, consistent with the half-power boundary.

    Practice

    1. If dish diameter doubles while wavelength, efficiency, and a small pointing error stay fixed, how do ideal gain and modeled pointing loss change?

    Gain scales as D²; the pointing-loss formula contains inverse beamwidth squared.

    Ideal gain rises by a factor of four, about 6.02 dB. Beamwidth roughly halves, making the modeled pointing-loss value in dB four times as large, within the approximation's main-beam range.
